report:
Regelrechter Artikulation im rechten Kniegelenk. Geringe T2 Signalanhebung im medialen Tibiaplateau (5/20). Ansonsten unauffälliges Knochenmarkssignal. Patella zentriert stehend. Regelrechter Knorpelbelag retropatellar.
Chronische Chondropathie medial femorotibial im Randbereich bei dort aufgebrauchtem Knorpelbelag. Korbhenkelrisses Innenmeniskus mit in die Notch umgeschlagenem Anteil (5/22 oder 3/115).
Außenmeniskus intakt. Vorderes Kreuzband am Ursprung gering T2 signalangehoben (4/19) jedoch durchgehend abgrenzbar. Hinteres Kreuzband unauffällig. Signalanhebung der ventromedialen Gelenkkapsel (z. B. 4/25), DD bei Partialläsion. Kollateralbandapparat intakt. Hämarthros. Kleine Plica mediopatellaris.
Umgebende Muskulatur unauffällig. Diffuse Flüssigkeitseinlagerungen/Einblutungen in die umgebende Subcutis

Exam Type: MRI KNEE LEFT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: Left knee pain
Comparison: Radiograph [DATE]

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the left knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture or bone bruise. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions.

JOINT SPACE:
Small joint effusion. No intra-articular bodies. Small Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: No meniscal tear or extrusion. Mild intrasubstance degeneration of the posterior horn.
Medial compartment cartilage: Mild loss of cartilage along the weightbearing aspect of the mediofemoral condyle.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Lateral compartment cartilage: Mild loss of cartilage along the lateral femoral condyle.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: Small partial-thickness cartilage defect along the lateral patellar facet.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Intact.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal. 
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Increased tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 19 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Imaged tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear. There is mild edema deep to the sartorius and gracilis tendons at the level of the knee joint which may represent bursitis.

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:

1. Mild compartmental knee osteoarthritis.
2. Intrasubstance degeneration of the posterior horn of the medial meniscus without evidence of tear.
3. Mild nonspecific edema deep to the sartorius and gracilis tendons may represent mild bursitis at the level of the knee joint.

EXAM TYPE: MRI KNEE RIGHT WO CONTRAST
EXAM DATE AND TIME: [DATE] [TIME]
INDICATION:     [IDENTIFIER]         
COMPARISON: None

IMPRESSION:  Probable bone contusion involving the lateral femoral condyle and lateral tibial plateau without discrete fracture line. Possible associated cortical/cartilaginous disruption along the lateral aspect of the intercondylar notch. Longitudinal tear of the posterior horn medial meniscus.

TECHNIQUE: MR imaging of the right knee was performed without intravenous contrast material.     

FINDINGS:

The ACL and PCL are intact.

In the medial compartment, there is a longitudinal tear of the anterior third of the posterior horn of the medial meniscus (images 6 through 8, series 4). The meniscus otherwise appears intact. There is no cartilaginous thinning or subchondral edema. The medial collateral ligament is intact.

In the lateral compartment, the lateral meniscus is intact. There is subchondral edema involving the lateral aspect of the lateral femoral condyle. There is no discrete fracture line. There is minimal edema in the adjacent lateral tibial plateau. There is no evidence of cartilaginous defect in the lateral compartment. The lateral collateral ligament is intact. 

In the patellofemoral compartment, the extensor mechanism is intact. Adjacent to the marrow edema in the lateral femoral condyle, there is the suggestion of disruption of the normal T2 hypointense cortical line along the lateral aspect of the intercondylar notch, best seen on image 22 of series 3, with possible defect in the adjacent articular cartilage (images 21 and 22, series 3). The retinacula appear within normal limits.

A physiologic amount of joint fluid is present. There is edema in the soft tissues just superficial to the lateral femoral condyle, suggesting contusion. No other periarticular soft tissue abnormalities are seen.

Antecedentes Clínicos:
Obs. Fractura por stress medial de la rodilla izquierda.
Hallazgos:
No hay alteraciones de señal significativas de la médula ósea.
Ligamentos cruzados y colaterales dentro de límites normales.
Meniscos de morfología y señal conservada, sin criterios categóricos de rotura.
Cartílagos de los compartimentos femorotibiales y de la tróclea femoral sin alteraciones. Finas
úlceras de espesor parcial del cartílago de la faceta lateral de la rótula, sin cambios óseos
secundarios.
No hay derrame articular. Pequeño quiste poplíteo sin signos de complicación.
Leve aumento de señal de la inserción distal del tendón cuadricipital, sin signos de rotura. Edema
el paquete adiposo retro cuadricipital suprarrotuliano, probablemente reactivo. Leve
engrosamiento y aumento de señal del tercio proximal del tendón rotuliano, sin signos de rotura.
Edema las partes blandas entre la banda iliotibial y el cóndilo femoral lateral.
No hay alteraciones de señal de la grasa de Hoffa.
Impresión:
Condropatía lesiones grado 2 de la rótula.
Pequeño quiste poplíteo no complicado.
Leve tendinosis cuadricipital distal con edema del paquete adiposo retro cuadricipital
suprarrotuliano, probablemente reactiva.
Leve tendinosis rotuliana proximal.
Fenómenos sugerentes de fricción de la banda iliotibial, correlacionar con clínica

Exam Type: MRI KNEE RIGHT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: Six-week history of knee pain associated with hockey localized to the anterior knee. No prior surgery.
Comparison: [REDACTED].

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the right knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture or bone bruise. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions. Mild to moderate osteoarthritis of the proximal tibiofibular joint characterized by marginal osteophyte formation, chondrosis and mild subchondral bone marrow edema.

JOINT SPACE:
Small joint effusion. There is a new 1.1 cm ossified intra-articular body localized posterior to the PCL (series 4, image 12). No Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Medial compartment cartilage: High-grade partial-thickness cartilage loss about the central and posterior weightbearing medial femoral condyle with superimposed areas of full-thickness fissuring and mild subchondral marrow edema, progressed from prior.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Lateral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: Full-thickness fissuring involving the median ridge and lateral patellar facet with mild subchondral marrow edema and cystic change, low-grade partial-thickness loss along the medial patellar facet peripherally. Focal full-thickness fissuring involving the mid to inferior lateral femoral trochlea with mild subchondral marrow edema superimposed on diffuse high-grade partial-thickness cartilage loss along the lateral femoral trochlea. [REDACTED].

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: Mild distal quadriceps insertional tendinosis. No tendon tear.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 13 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
Moderate prepatellar bursitis. No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:
1.	Progressive patellofemoral greater than medial tibiofemoral compartment chondrosis.
2.	Small joint effusion with new 1.1 cm ossified intra-articular body posterior to the PCL.
3.	Mild distal quadriceps insertional tendinosis without tear.
4.	Moderate prepatellar bursitis.

Findings: There is a minor knee effusion. Normal medial and lateral menisci. No evidence of tears.  Normal ACL, PCL, MCL and LCL. Normal extensor mechanism.  The tibiofemoral and patellofemoral articular cartilage is unremarkable. No evidence of cartilage degeneration or loss. There is a small focal sclerotic lesion in the medial distal femoral metaphysis. This was previously seen on x-ray dated [DATE].  
Conclusion: No significant abnormality.

Findings:  Comparison is made to previous MRI dated [DATE].  There is a mild knee effusion. The known complex tear of the posterior horn of the medial meniscus with a flipped fragment posteromedially is again noted and remains unchanged compared to previous. Normal appearances of the lateral meniscus.  Normal ACL, PCL, MCL and LCL. Normal quadriceps tendon and patellar ligament.   The patella is mildly high lying. T T T G distance is mildly widened and measures 17mm. The patella lies in a mildly lateralized position . Moderate patellar articular degeneration is noted, more so in the caudal aspect of the lateral patellar facet. Mild underlying bony change is noted. The trochlear articular cartilage is preserved.  The tibiofemoral articular cartilage is unremarkable.  
Conclusion: Complex tear of the posterior horn of the medial meniscus with a flipped fragment as described. This is unchanged compared to previous. Patellar maltracking with patellar chondropathy as described.

Unauffälliges Knochenmarksignal. Kreuzbänder intakt. Kollateralbänder intakt. Schräg-horizontale Rissbildung im Innenmeniskushinterhorn bei mukoider Vorschädigung (7/8). Flächige mäßige Chondropathie femoral mit dorsal vollschichtem Knorpeldefekt von ap 12 x ml 8 mm (5/26). Oberflächliche Chondropathie im lateralen Kompartiment. Flächig vollschichtige Chondropathie an der medialen Patellafacette sowie an der korrespondierenden Trochlea und am Sulcus trochlearis. Ausgeprägte Gelenkerguss mit synovialen Proliferationen. Plica mediopatellaris am ehesten Typ B nach Sakakibara. Weichteile unauffällig.
